title: Inline actions
summary: A link-style action at text height, in a row that wraps, a table cell and a sentence, with a touch area that never overlaps its neighbours.

try.label: Tap an action in a wrapped row
Tap an action in a table row

purpose: Button size="inline" (the bundled primitive): a link label at text height whose 44 px touch area is a pseudo-element. It reaches into the room the layout leaves and no further, so in a row that wraps onto two lines a tap always lands on the button that shows under the finger. Four French actions of different lengths wrap in a narrow row that declares its gaps (--inline-gap-x, --inline-gap-y, set next to the row's own gap); the same row with nothing declared; one inline button per table cell; one in a sentence. Scripted, no model.
notes: On a phone each inline button's tap area is 44 px high and at least 44 wide where the layout leaves room, and no two areas share a pixel: the last action of the first line and the first action of the second line each handle their own tap. A row that declares nothing gets no extension beyond its text line (it never overlaps, it just has no 44 px floor); the fix for that is to give the row its gap, not to size the button. An isolated button (a table cell, a sentence) keeps the full 44 px.

flows.name: Tap an action in a wrapped row

steps.say: Tap “Modifier la facture”, the last action of the first line
steps.expect: That action handles the tap, not the one below it.

steps.say: Tap “Relancer le client”, the first action of the second line
steps.expect: That action handles the tap, not the one above it.

flows.name: Tap an action in a table row

steps.expect: The first row's action handles the tap.
The second row's action handles it, not the first.
